fov360.options.title: 360 FOV Settings
fov360.options.splitScreen.tooltip: Splits the window into forward and rear halves, each using the full FOV. Intended for two monitors at 180° to create a seamless full-sphere view.
fov360.options.invertSplitScreen.tooltip: Swaps the forward and rear halves and the side the GUI is displayed on.
fov360.options.faceSizeCap.tooltip: Maximum resolution of each cubemap face. Higher values improve quality at high FOVs but use more VRAM.
fov360.options.lowResTopBottomFaces.tool: Renders the top and bottom capture faces at lower resolution, except the face currently being viewed.
fov360.options.editThresholds.tooltip: Choose which projection is used at each FOV and how the view blends between them.
fov360.options.reset.tooltip: Resets every 360 FOV setting, including the FOV thresholds, to its default.
fov360.options.reset.confirm: Reset all 360 FOV settings to their defaults?
fov360.thresholds.title: FOV Thresholds
fov360.thresholds.help:
Pick combination of projections to blend.
Click to add a point, drag to move, right-click to delete. Dashed line is your FOV.
fov360.thresholds.pointHint: Drag to move, right-click to remove
fov360.thresholds.addHint: Click to add a point here
fov360.thresholds.setFovHint: Right-click to set your FOV here
fov360.thresholds.keysHint: Left and right arrows move the selected point by 1°, or 10° with Shift. Delete removes it. Right-click the bar outside a point to set your FOV there.
fov360.thresholds.blend.tooltip: How the view changes from %s to %s between the previous point and this one.
fov360.thresholds.blend.first: The first point has no earlier point to blend from. Its projection is used for every FOV below it.
fov360.thresholds.info: Point %s of %s (max %s). Arrow keys move the selected point by 1°, or 10° with Shift.
fov360.thresholds.preview.tooltip: Removes the blur and darkening behind this screen so the world shows through while you edit.
fov360.thresholds.reset.confirm: Reset the FOV thresholds to their defaults?
